describes: What grows on and over the town's ground in October 1989, and how it is drawn: where lichen and moss take on rock (blender/generators/growth.py, on_rock), the crusts' and the moss's painted values (Shaders/GrowthPaint.hlsl), and the tufts of heath and weeds (blender/parts/growth/tufts.py) with their densities per habitat (blender/generators/growth.py, place_tufts). Where they grow, and since when, is the record's; how they look on this coast in this month is this file's.

heather.what: ling (Calluna), browned after flowering: stiff, wiry twigs fanning up from a woody base, darker at the base, rust-brown tips

summer.what: in July, before it flowers: dark grey-green shoots, lighter and greener at their tips

juniper.what: common juniper, dark and upright: flame-shaped shoots, nearly black in fog

heathGrass.what: wavy hair-grass and purple moor-grass gone to straw: fine blades, straw tips over a darker base

summer.what: in July, flowering: green leaves under silvery straw panicles

turf.what: summer turf on thin till (sheep's fescue, common bent, sweet vernal grass): a mat of fine blades, yellow-green where the sun takes their tips, a few gone to straw, over a darker green thatch

yardGrass.what: long yard grass (cocksfoot, Yorkshire fog, couch) uncut since 1986: tall, lodged, straw-tipped, some seed heads standing

pathGrass.what: short grass coming back over a path still walked now and then

willowherb.what: rosebay willowherb gone to seed: bare red stems standing in a stand, split pods curling at the top with white seed fluff caught in them

heath.what: coastal heath come back since the sheep went (1958): heather the matrix, hair-grass in the gaps, a juniper here and there

yard.what: a yard let go since 1986: long grass over it all, willowherb in stands along the walls and the edge

tipTurf.what: the Holm tip's thin till: summer turf over it all, wavy hair-grass in tussocks through it, heather in patches where the till is thinnest

path.what: the path to the door grassing over: short grass, thinnest down the middle

notes.rock: on_rock's rules (interface-growth-rock.md): lichen wants the open, rain-washed faces: none on a face leaning out past overhang (the normal's up), full from fullRain, times the sky it sees to skyPower. The damp foot (the height over its ground, m) takes moss over lichen: lichen from footLichen[0] to full at [1], moss full at footMoss[0] to none at [1], at most footMossMax. A joint (m to the nearest): no lichen inside jointLip, moss from full at jointMoss[0] to none at [1]. A low north face with little sky: moss up to northMossMax as an upright face's sky falls from northShade[0] to [1]. Moss fills in over mossYearsFull years; where it grows it takes mossOverLichen of the lichen's place. Rates and the delay before the first crust are growth.py's (LICHEN_DELAY).
notes.painted: How the crusts and the moss show in the painted corner (the art-direction page, The growth: flat crusts that follow the rock, matte, within 5 L* of their surface at blue hour, never mounds; a few broad value shifts, never noise). lichen.ratio: the crust's albedo over its rock's (1.4: a face at L* 11 reads 14, a top at 22 reads 26.5), a touch warmer and greener. A century's quiet surface is covered to shareMax, reached at fullYears. A crust grows out from where it took, so it is drawn as colonies: discs with a lobed edge that merge into scalloped patches where they crowd (reference 15), two sizes (spacing: m between the big ones and the small ones; smallShare: the small ones' part of the cover), their edge bitten by lobe (size m, depth of a radius), soft its least softness (of a spacing). They cluster (cluster: the clusters' size m, how much they vary the share, and how sharply they part, 0 to 1), so a face takes a few broad shifts. The big ones are the shapes and hold past the focus; the small ones and the lobes are marks, gone past it (their share given to the big), where the edge softens to softFar (of a spacing); the big ones keep their own outline at every distance (outline: its bumps' size m and how far they bite, of a cell), so none is a circle. Once a colony spans a few pixels, it is seen as its share. moss.ratio: darker and greener than its stone (a pigment: the joint's dark is the light's); patch its shapes' size, soft their edge.
notes.tufts: levels: each level's reach from the eye (m), crossfaded over fade of it. thin: past from (m) the far tufts thin out, a quarter kept at 120 m, the kept ones widened (the far heath as fewer, bigger clumps; Ghost of Tsushima doubles a far tile's size at the same count). budget: the most triangles a tuft of any species may have at each level, the most tufts per m² of any habitat, and the corner's whole draw (triangles and tufts in either final view); blender/parts/growth/corner.py prints them and fails over any. species: heights and widths (m), blades per level, segments per blade per level, a blade's width at its base (m), lean (how far a blade tips from upright, 0 to 1, from the clump's middle out), curl (how far its tip bends over), base and tip (sRGB, its root and its tip: dark to light, Ghost of Tsushima), clumpHue (how much one clump's hue differs from the next: slight). habitats: the species' shares, tufts per m² at the fullest, and clump: the patches' size (m) and how far between them the cover drops (0 none, 1 bare); a yard's lip: how near its edge (m) the long grass falls out over it, how far it leans there (rad), and how much taller it stands at the edge (never thinned there: the rankest grass is where no one treads); lipRow: a row of it along the lip itself, a tuft every so many m, set in from the edge by between these (m), so the edge is a fringe. A species' season (`summer`) is its colours then, over its own; damp its tips' colour where the ground stays damp (a stone's shed). A habitat's patch: where another mix takes over (heather where the till is thinnest), a seeded field over cellM cut at its share, its edge crisp over edgeM (m), ragged by rag, its tufts scaled by scale, every foot kept if full (a mat). Its ground: the map under its tufts (growth.ground_map), the sward's colour drier toward dry over dryShare of it, the patch's colour where a patch stands, varied by vary over varyM, marked by clumps over clumpM (a stroke with the wind) and a grain over grainM [across, along]; the tufts' roots take its colour (look.upNormal: how far the clump's dome is lit as the ground's up).
